Recommendation: do not make a blanket purchase of local AI hardware. Keep hosted models as the default for most product and internal workloads, and reserve local hardware for a small set of cases where data residency, latency, or air-gap requirements make hosted inference unacceptable. The main reason is that local hardware shifts a predictable, variable cost into a fixed, operational one: procurement, racks, power, cooling, monitoring, patching, model updates, and staffing. Hosted models already absorb much of that burden, and their pricing is usually easier to forecast at the workload level even if it is less predictable at the token level.

The strongest case for local hardware is control. If we handle regulated data, customer-identifiable content, or prompts that cannot leave the environment, a local deployment can reduce exposure and simplify compliance
